Test Objective: Verify PCIe device enumeration by performing link training, cache coherency programming, link status polling, vendor ID read, command register configuration, memory base programming, BAR enumeration on both DM0 and DM1 instances, and synchronization handshake.
Test Description: This test validates the complete PCIe device enumeration flow. It begins by initializing the synchronization register and performing link training on the configured PCIe instance (DM0 or DM1 in RC or EP mode). Cache coherency control is then programmed on both PCIE0 and PCIE1 instances by setting the master AXI read/write cache mode and value fields via read-modify-write operations on the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register. The test polls the SII link status registers on both instances until the link is confirmed up (status bits 0xD1). In RC mode, the Vendor ID is read from the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG, the TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG is configured to enable IO, Memory, and Bus Master access, and memory base programming is performed for both DM0 and DM1. System-level configuration registers are then written. Cache coherency is subsequently disabled by clearing the cache value fields. BAR enumeration is performed on both slave interfaces by writing 0xFFFFFFFF to BAR0_REG through PREF_MEM_LIMIT_PREF_MEM_BASE_REG, reading back to determine BAR sizes, then programming final BAR values. The test concludes by polling the synchronization register for a completion handshake value of 0x12345678.
Pre-conditions:
1. PCIe subsystem is powered on and out of reset.
2. PCIe link partner (RC or EP) is present and ready.
3. The compile-time mode flag (DM0_RC, DM1_RC, DM0_EP, or DM1_EP) is defined.
4. System integration interface (SII) registers are accessible.
5. PCIe DBI and slave configuration spaces are accessible.
6. Header file pcie.h with macro definitions and helper functions is available.
Test Steps:
1. Write 0x0 to the synchronization register (0xE6004100) to initialize the handshake.
2. Perform PCIe link training on the configured instance (DM0 or DM1) with x4 lane width.
3. Program cache coherency on PCIE0: read COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF, set AXI write cache mode bits [14:11] to 0xF and read cache mode bits [6:3] to 0xF via read-modify-write, then set AXI write cache value bits [30:27] to 0xF and read cache value bits [22:19] to 0xF.
4. Repeat cache coherency programming for PCIE1 instance.
5. Wait 20 cycles, then perform consolidated cache coherency write on both PCIE0 and PCIE1.
6. Poll SII0 link status register (0xC0) until link-up status bits (0xD1) are confirmed.
7. Configure non-secure protection via NIC programming.
8. Poll SII1 link status register (0xC0) until link-up status bits (0xD1) are confirmed.
9. In RC mode: Read TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG (0x0) to retrieve Vendor ID.
10. In RC mode: Write 0x7 to TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG (0x4) to enable IO, Memory, Bus Master.
11. In RC mode: Execute memory base programming for DM0 and DM1.
12. Write 0x1 to six system-level configuration registers (0xE690000C-0xE6900034).
13. Disable cache coherency on PCIE0: clear AXI cache value bits while keeping mode bits.
14. Repeat cache disable on PCIE1.
15. Perform BAR enumeration on slave interface 1: write 0xFFFFFFFF to BAR0-PREF_MEM registers, read back BAR sizes, program final values.
16. Repeat BAR enumeration on slave interface 0.
17. Poll synchronization register until 0x12345678 is received.
18. Call finish(0) to end the test.
Expected Results:
1. Link training completes successfully on the configured PCIe instance.
2. Cache coherency control fields are correctly programmed and verified on both PCIE0 and PCIE1.
3. SII0 and SII1 link status registers report link-up status (bits matching 0xD1).
4. Vendor ID read returns expected value (0x16C3 per spec reset value).
5. Command register is successfully written with IO, Memory, and Bus Master enable bits.
6. Memory base programming completes without errors.
7. System-level configuration registers accept writes.
8. Cache coherency is successfully disabled on both instances.
9. BAR enumeration on both slave interfaces returns valid BAR size information.
10. Final BAR address values are programmed and read back correctly.
11. Synchronization register reaches 0x12345678.
12. Test completes with finish(0) indicating PASS.

Functional Area: PCIe DMA Write and Read Data Transfer
Test Objective: Verify PCIe DMA write and read data transfer across all four channels (CH0-CH3) on both DM0 and DM1 instances, including interrupt-driven completion handling, data preloading, and synchronization handshake.
Test Description: This test validates PCIe DMA write and read operations across all four DMA channels. It begins by initializing the synchronization register and performing link training. After link-up is confirmed via SII polling, the Vendor ID is read and the command register is configured. BAR and memory base programming are performed. Source memory is preloaded with test patterns (0xC0DEBEED and 0xF00DDEAF). GIC interrupt handling is configured. DMA write interrupt mask and read interrupt mask registers are cleared to enable interrupts. For each of the four channels (CH0-CH3), the DMA write channel is programmed and the write doorbell register is written to initiate the transfer. The test waits for interrupt-driven completion via the Default_IRQHandler. After all write channels complete, the same sequence is performed for DMA read channels (CH0-CH3) using the read doorbell register. The IRQ handler reads DMA write/read interrupt status registers, clears interrupts via the interrupt clear registers, and acknowledges via GIC. The test concludes with finish(0).
Pre-conditions:
1. PCIe subsystem is powered on and out of reset.
2. PCIe link partner (RC or EP) is present and ready.
3. DM0_RC or DM1_RC compile-time flag is defined.
4. GIC interrupt controller is functional.
5. DMA engine is enabled and channels are available.
6. Source and destination memory regions are accessible.
7. Header file pcie.h with macro definitions and helper functions is available.

Functional Area: PCIe Register Write/Read and Reset Value Verification
Test Objective: Verify register reset default values and write/read functionality for PCIe RC controller registers (MSI_CAP, PORT_LOGIC), SII registers (TRANSMIT_HEADER, PHY_CONTROL), and PHY registers across both PCIE0 and PCIE1 instances.
Test Description: This test validates register reset values and write/read integrity across three register domains: (1) RC controller DBI registers (MSI_CAP_OFF_08H_REG, MSI_CAP_OFF_10H_REG, FILTER_MASK_2_OFF, AXI_MSTR_MSG_ADDR_HIGH_OFF, UTILITY_OFF) on both PCIE0 and PCIE1; (2) SII registers (TRANSMIT_HEADER2, TRANSMIT_HEADER3, PHY_CONTROL_23) on both instances; (3) PHY registers at absolute addresses (0xE68860B8, 0xE68862B8, 0xE68864B8 for PHY0; 0xE68A60B8, 0xE68A62B8, 0xE68A64B8 for PHY1). The chk_rst_val() function reads all registers and compares against expected default values (0x0 for all). PHY reset is asserted via SII_PHY_RST_CONTROL before PHY register reads. The chk_rd_wr() function writes three test patterns (0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555) to all registers, then reads back and compares. SII registers are masked with write masks before comparison. PHY registers use separate test patterns (0x7BAF, 0x1, 0x003B) and a 0x1FFF write mask. The test reports pass/fail based on accumulated error counts (err1, err2).
Pre-conditions:
1. PCIe subsystem is powered on and out of reset.
2. PCIe DBI registers are accessible without link training.
3. SII registers are accessible.
4. PHY registers are accessible after PHY reset assertion.
5. Header file pcie.h with macro definitions is available.
6. No link training is required for this register-level test.

1. Call chk_rst_val() to verify reset default values.

4. Read all 3 SII0 registers (TRANSMIT_HEADER2, TRANSMIT_HEADER3, PHY_CONTROL_23) and compare against default 0x0.
5. Read all 3 SII1 registers and compare against default 0x0.

8. Read 3 PHY0 registers (0xE68860B8, 0xE68862B8, 0xE68864B8) and compare against default 0x0.
9. Read 3 PHY1 registers (0xE68A60B8, 0xE68A62B8, 0xE68A64B8) and compare against default 0x0.

13. Read back all RC1 registers and compare against written pattern.
14. Read back all SII0 registers and compare against masked pattern.
